correctness.rationale: A landmark set fails precisely when it is a subset of some pair bisector, so a largest failure is a whole largest bisector. On the nonempty support where the endpoints differ, the independent Hamming-distance increments have atom masses 1/q, (q−2)/q, 1/q. For q≥4 the unique modal atom is 0, and fixing any other active coordinate gives a nonzero complementary sum with positive probability, making the modal bound strict. On a wholly binary support the central binomial mass is zero for odd support and decreases strictly through even sizes starting at two. A ternary increment bounds the probability by 1/3, with equality exactly when there are at most one other active coordinate (otherwise the other increments can all be +1). Comparing these sharp bounds gives the six cases, including the empty bisector for the lone K₂. On the maximizing supports, avoiding the offending pair gives the singleton-coordinate slabs; the binary pair gives either parity; the ternary pair pairs the unused letters and the crossed endpoint letters, giving all six permutations; the mixed pair gives six injective two-row matchings. Essential-coordinate support is intrinsic and the patterns within each support differ, so the labeled counts, including the homogeneous corollaries, follow. The supporting verifier tests size and number by finite distance-mask enumeration; the universal conclusions here are from the proof, not that recorded finite check.
